description: Check the original suspicion that document-conditioned TopicAttack generation itself violates the no-user-instruction knowledge boundary.

scope.paper_version: TopicAttack, EMNLP 2025 final, Section 3 and Section 4.2
scope.experiment_arm: Released default chatbot attack construction using attack_prompt_transfer.txt
scope.configuration: Static source boundary only: default GPTChatbot, default empty chatbot_system.txt, default transition template. Independent user-instruction access is a separate required claim; no historical runtime assertions.

rules.reference: https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.372.pdf#page=4 (Section 3, Attackers Knowledge, continued from PDF page 3)

claim: The default chatbot attack-generation request violates the declared knowledge boundary merely by including the benign document text.

policy_application.reference: https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.372.pdf#page=4 (Section 3, Attackers Knowledge, continued from PDF page 3)
policy_application.reason: Section 3 expressly permits the attacker to know the benign content being injected. This rule applies to document content, not to the separate original user-instruction field.

delivery.reason: construct_attack.py formats d_item[input] into the default transition template and passes the rendered message to model.respond. This is a bound source-level input path, not merely a dataset field existing and not a saved model request.

refutation.reference: https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.372.pdf#page=4 (Section 3, Attackers Knowledge, continued from PDF page 3)
refutation.reason: The named suspicion mistakes explicitly permitted document visibility for prohibited access to the original user instruction. Permission refutes this specific access claim, without asserting global paper consistency.

description: Check whether the original user-instruction field is independently delivered in the default chatbot construction messages.

scope.paper_version: TopicAttack, EMNLP 2025 final, Section 3 and Section 4.2
scope.experiment_arm: Released default chatbot generation request, including its wrapper and empty system prompt
scope.artifact_revision: LukeChen-go/topicattack 2aced58ad6f3587c8ba064b5e5cad74a29ef41de; chatbot.py SHA256 21fd3e1323bc7279cad32ccf36bd0b88f69c0c50baeb9fae5f918f201dcbf0e4; default chatbot_system.txt empty SHA256 e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855
scope.configuration: Full direct request-construction boundary only. construct_attack.py reads the default template and passes a rendered string; GPTChatbot.respond constructs messages from that string plus the empty default system prompt. No custom template/system, natural-language inference, other generator, or historical-run claim.

rules.reference: https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.372.pdf#page=4 (Section 3, Attackers Knowledge, continued from PDF page 3)

claim: The released default chatbot constructor sends d_item[instruction] as an independent input to the auxiliary attack-generation LLM.

policy_application.reference: https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.372.pdf#page=4 (Section 3, Attackers Knowledge, continued from PDF page 3)
policy_application.reason: The no-original-user-input restriction applies to the attack-generation LLM in this declared construction setting. The separate allowed benign-document input is not reclassified as a query.

delivery.reason: Positive request-boundary proof: the constructor renders only input, attacker injection, attacker target topic and fixed turn count; the selected template contains those slots; GPTChatbot.respond sends only the supplied rendered string and the empty default system string. No instruction-field slot or conversation-history append exists on this selected direct path. The enclosing dataset object may still store instruction for evaluation. This does not exclude inference of task facts from allowed content.

refutation.reason: The alleged independent instruction-field delivery is excluded by the complete selected message-construction path, not by a repository-wide failed text search. The conclusion is limited to this default direct request.

description: Check the suspicion that choosing a sensitive topic for an explicit-memory training seed is itself forbidden exact-future-task access.

scope.experiment_arm: Topic-conditioned explicit-memory seed construction during adaptive training
scope.configuration: Static explicit-memory branch with nonempty attack_goal and tax in its description. Only topic selection is judged here. The separate source path that passes a concrete training user_message to the mutator is acknowledged and is not relabelled topic-only.

claim: The explicit-memory offline seed builder violates the declared boundary merely by conditioning a seed on the configured tax topic.

policy_application.reason: Section 4.1 explicitly defines attack generation for a selected topic, backend and defense. That positive topic-conditioned procedure applies to this offline seed branch. No permission for arbitrary exact future test queries is inferred.

delivery.reason: The explicit-memory branch invokes _build_explicit_seed_emails; this helper derives a topic phrase from attack_goal.description and inserts that category into seed templates. This source-level path confirms the category input for the named operation, not the absence of concrete training queries elsewhere.

refutation.reason: The named allegation treats the documented topic condition as prohibited user-query access. The paper explicitly authorizes this topic-conditioned attack-generation procedure, refuting that narrow allegation.

description: Check a single fixed released train_0 to test_0 tax/rag/none pair rather than all Trojan Hippo historical executions.

scope.paper_version: Trojan Hippo, arXiv:2605.01970v1, Section 4.1 train/test separation
scope.experiment_arm: One released tax/rag/none train_0 and test_0 01.json pair plus the fixed-payload propagation step
scope.artifact_revision: debesheedas/trojan-hippo-benchmark ebeb739dada097e06b125faa70e82e064482b64b; train-file SHA256 251810fae0cd0407e0f84600283fd17370483d8d27dc3c8ee55de5f76444593c; test-file SHA256 3a6593de0187682ebafe796ad0967a7e5791a9abfd226033458cec30234ee169
scope.configuration: Static one-pair transfer boundary only, no --adaptive test execution. Released step-4 query hashes differ: train dbf1d4b57701d08b056ec9e04fc0f63553715fd0d1887b04560648707ebcad1a; test 48c231234016a5cd642cc347f5f710aca6187dd89ca1769a4f644c89cbd0e480. Attack-email objects have identical sorted-key JSON SHA256 6d762ce840cd455e8027b47d06a26fff010eb07e8f671b97a5efd1bdde302740. This does not establish absence of test-query leakage in all branches or historical runs.

target.phase: fixed-payload transfer for one released train/test pair

edge.phase: fixed-payload transfer for one released train/test pair

claim: The fixed propagation step for the released train_0/tax/rag/none/01.json to test_0/tax/rag/none/01.json pair feeds the held-out test trigger query back into attack-payload mutation.

policy_application.reason: No prohibition is invented from the inability to modify user queries. The suspected transfer of a training-query input to this distinct test instance is refuted at the selected propagation boundary; the training mutator and held-out transfer are different phases and instances.

delivery.reason: Positive boundary evidence: propagation chooses an existing attack using training caches and grouping metadata, then replaces only insert_attack_email.attack_email; it makes no mutator request with the test trigger. The selected released pair has a different train and test trigger query and the same attack-email object. The exact training user_message path elsewhere therefore is not evidence of delivery of this test query.

refutation.reason: The cited concrete training query and the named held-out query are distinct instances, and the selected transfer operation excludes the claimed regeneration input. This refutes only this one-pair propagation allegation, not future-query acquisition across the paper.
